newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany agrees measures against Scientology.
newsitem.headline: Germany agrees measures against Scientology.

text.p: Germany's federal and regional governments agreed measures at a meeting on Wednesday to counter what they called the "expansionist aims and claim to domination" of the Church of Scientology.

The package aimed to establish a unified approach against the U.S.-based group after a number of politicians and regional states called for action against what they allege is a profit-making, pseudo-religious sect relying on manipulation.

"The federal and state governments agree that the dubious activities of the Scientology organisation and its expansionist aims and claim to domination must be countered determinedly with all legal means," the governments said in a statement.

The move prompted an angry response from Scientology, which rejected the accusations in a statement and called the measures a "testimony to inadequacy" intended to "spread the propaganda of official church extremists".

The group said "systematic discrimination" against Scientology in Germany had been condemned by the United Nations Human Rights Committee, the Organisation for Security and Coooperation in Europe (OSCE) and the U.S. State Department.
Scientology has drawn fire from several quarters in Germany, especially the state of Bavaria and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats.

Bonn has published a booklet warning of the dangers of the organisation and Bavaria is making state employees fill out a questionnaire detailing their ties to organisation. It has called for Scientologists to be banned from public service.
On Wednesday, the authorities agreed to consider putting Scientology under surveillance by the anti-extremist Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV).
The governments also agreed to exclude Scientologists as far as legally possible from public contracts for installations requiring a special degree of trust, such as education and advice centres.
They said they would also consider legal regulation of groups offering people, on a commercial basis, help in coping with their lives.

The Bonn government set up an inter-ministerial working group to coordinate activities relating to Scientology and pledged to continue "emphatically to counter the Scientology Organisation's disinformation campaigns internationally".

Scientology, founded in 1954 by American science fiction writer L. Ron Hubbard, gives would-be members personality tests and then offers courses and literature to help them realise what the church sees as their full potential.

Germany has stricter regulations on church status than the United States and has refused to register Scientology as a religion. The group says it has around 30,000 members in Germany though the government puts the figure between 10,000 and 20,000.
